previous_headings: STEP1 - Opcion A: Download data from URL
title: Download raw data from public sources
text: can download antibiogram files NCBI, ENA, BV-BRC using reference file available Zenodo, published July 4, 2025 (version 4). can compress file .gz format loading R. read_tsv() function supports reading .gz-compressed files directly. recommend simplifying column formats using janitor package standardizing column names shown .
code: library(here) # Define URL and local destination anti_url <- "https://zenodo.org/records/15809334/files/antibiograms.tsv.zip" # Replace "inst/extdata" with the actual path to your folder targetfile <- here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv.zip") # <- Change this to your own directory  # Download the compressed file download.file(url = anti_url, destfile = targetfile, mode = "wb")  # Unzip the .zip file unzip(targetfile, exdir = "inst/extdata")  # Import the data into R antibiograms_metadata <- readr::read_tsv(here("inst/extdata","antibiograms.tsv"))  # <- Specify the directory path # Compress the file to .gz format original_file <- here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv") gz_file <- here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv.gz") R.utils::gzip(original_file, destname = gz_file, overwrite = TRUE)  # Read the .tsv.gz file into R antibiograms_metadata <- readr::read_tsv(here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv.gz")) library(janitor)  # Clean antibiogram metadata antibiograms_db <- antibiograms_metadata %>%   # Standardizes column names: converts them to lowercase,   # replaces spaces and special characters with underscores   janitor::clean_names() %>%    # Renames the columns   rename(     accession = reads,     scientific_name_Antibiogram = species   )

title: Curated Resource for Antimicrobial Resistance Data Exploration
text: goal AMRdb provide curated, high-quality dataset supports analysis, visualization, modeling antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Specifically, AMRdb enables researchers data scientists : Analyze outputs Machine Learning (ML) Deep Learning (DL) models, particularly related MIC (Minimum Inhibitory Concentration) predictions phenotypic classification (Resistant, Intermediate, Susceptible). Explore clinical genomic metadata associated microbial isolates. Integrate structured data reproducible workflows computational AMR surveillance comparative genomics.
